card: Configures Guix to build official Linux x86_64 and aarch64 release binaries (excluding GUI tools) as static position-independent executables (-static-pie) using glibc 2.44. This allows bitcoind and utilities to run without dynamic linker dependencies on non-glibc distributions like Alpine Linux and older distributions, resolving #19075. Patches applied to glibc remove non-deterministic Guix store paths and disable dlopen for NSS, meaning dynamic NSS modules like mDNS, LDAP, or SSSD will no longer resolve hosts. Post-build symbol and security check scripts are updated to assert the expected properties of static ELF executables.
changed_since_previous: Added a dedicated release note documenting the switch to -static-pie and highlighting that dynamic NSS modules (like mDNS, LDAP, or SSSD) will no longer function for host resolution.
evidence: PR description fixes #19075 ('build: Investigate aarch64 pointer authentication')
doc/release-notes-25573.md notes that binaries 'can now be run on non-glibc based systems, as well as on systems that ship with older glibcs than those previously supported'

doc/release-notes-25573.md documents the trade-off: 'A side-effect of this change is that name resolution through dynamic nss modules is not possible. Users using mdns (.local), LDAP, or SSSD to resolve names for local connections should verify that connections are still resolved correctly.'
problem: Linux release binaries dynamically link against glibc and the host dynamic linker, preventing them from running on non-glibc distributions like Alpine Linux and on systems with glibc versions older than the build toolchain. Dynamic linking also complicates security hardening mitigations such as aarch64 pointer authentication (#19075).

risk.why: Flaws in custom glibc patches, toolchain flags, or static linking could break release binaries or cause unexpected networking/DNS resolution failures for end users running official Linux releases.

scope_notes: Modifies the Guix build manifest and toolchain recipes to compile glibc 2.44 with custom patches that strip /gnu/store path references and disable dlopen in NSS. Also adapts symbol-check.py and security-check.py to validate static ELF executables.
summary: Configure Guix to build official Linux x86_64 and aarch64 non-GUI executables (bitcoind and CLI tools) as static position-independent executables (-static-pie) using glibc 2.44. Apply patches to glibc to eliminate non-deterministic Guix store paths and disable runtime dynamic loading in NSS modules. Adapt post-build symbol-check and security-check scripts to verify static ELF binaries.
